[win/linux/amiga/BeOS] ADOM has earned its reputation as one of the most prominent roguelikes

Well. I had a little unplanned hiatus there, I was switching ISPs and lost my connection for a while. I had originally planned to do a post about ADOM coinciding with the commercial release on Nov. 16... Feh. Still, the game is twenty years old. This post isn't that late, relatively speaking.

About the game: ADOM is one of the "core" roguelikes - when talking about the genre it’s one of those games which will definitely come up, it is older and larger and frankly better than most others and it’s one that most every roguelike fan has at least tried at some point.

I've talked more about it here, it turns out I've got a lot to say about ADOM.

Since this is a sub for free and complete games, what I linked in the title is the old site with the fully complete version of the game from 2002. The new version is available here and this is what I would recommend actually playing. It has audio, for one thing, and graphics if you're into that. It also has an advertisement for the commercial game, which leads to my one minor gripe with the new version, but it's not burdensome and there have certainly been a lot of improvements.

'Better' is subjective: I think nethack is much better, because it's gameplay is more balanced. Example: Dark elven priestess. They are an 'easy' monster which can instakill much stronger characters due to a paralyzing attack, which reliably hits characters up to a certain level(according to anecdotes), where no other elf or priest does the same, the only protection are rare items, and there is no in-game way to suspect this. It's an easy monster, but it's not one of the first monsters you encounter, by the time you see it you have fought numerous priests of other races and elves, and none have a similar attack. Monster memory doesn't warns you either.

In other words, unless you read a guide every time you find a new monster, you are guaranteed to die at least once, by design. No game (unless that's the point of the game) should require reading a guide to win; one thing is requiring luck/skill to win, another is to have at least 1 guaranteed death after many hours of gameplay.

Nethack (which I think it's the best roguelike) doesn't have this problem, and at least in DCSS forums it has been acknowledged that this specific situation is a problem and deliberately try to avoid it designing it into the game.

Well... there are a lot of insta-kill elements in many rogulikes, ADOM and Nethack both have them: drinking from a fountain in Nethack, for example, could spawn a water demon. That's almost certain death at low levels. In ADOM there's the banshee (equivalent to the gorgon in Nethack) or the chaos piranhas. The games drop hints about those things though (not the water demon). But I guess that's where you're distinguishing, isn't it? That there aren't any hints about enemies who can paralyze?

Okay, well maybe. I've certainly died to ghouls in ADOM many times due to paralyzation, but you're exaggerating when you say that every new enemy is a guaranteed death. Even enemies which paralyze. Also, learning to be careful about unknowns is something that you develop over time. I remember the first time I encountered a moloch - freaked me out. I couldn't hurt the thing at all and it hit like a truck. Actually, come to think of it, I can't remember if I survived that... I seem to recall getting trapped in a corridor. Maybe not the best example.

I'll grant that Nethack has fewer unavoidable deaths, though when they do happen I find them to be more frustrating. A gnome with a wand of death is worse, in my mind, than a ghoul (or dark eleven priestess, or claw bug) which has an innate ability to paralyze. At least the next time you see a priestess you know what's what. You don't expect gnomes to be death-spitting kill-bots.

That said, I stated specifically in the article that I didn't think ADOM was better than Nethack, just that I found it more compelling for a couple of reasons. And it's funny that you should bring up DCSS - I haven't played it since they changed the name, but back when it was called Linley Henzell's Dungeon Crawl it was much worse for this than either ADOM or Nethack. A lot of that due to the extreme potency of the ranged attacks of certain monsters. You could take a step and spot an ogre mage, for example, and be dead before you had the time to do anything because the mage had hit you with a crystal shard.
